m.nyanpasu_config.application.preference.description:
A patch of the ordinary preferences.

 An omitted field stays unchanged, and so does a field sent as `null`: for an ordinary
 preference `null` is a no-op, not a clear. Only `release_channel` treats an explicit `null`
 as "clear the value" (a double option), and `window_close` is a nested patch that names only
 the window kinds it changes.

 It is decoded only through the full patch ([`TryFrom`]), so unrelated unknown keys are ignored
 as before and a privileged field is refused instead of silently dropped.

m.nyanpasu_ipc.api.status.t.ConfigRevisi.description:
Identity of the config the running core actually adopted.

 `source_hash` is computed over the caller's own file and `effective_hash`
 over the canonical form the core is running, both FNV-1a over canonical
 YAML. A caller that holds the source file can therefore confirm the
 service read the same bytes it wrote, without reimplementing the hash.
 The manager's private runtime copy path is deliberately not exposed: it
 lives in a 0o700 directory the caller cannot read, so it would only
 mislead.

m.nyanpasu_ipc.api.status.t.CoreControll.description:
The core's control endpoint, as the manager resolved it.

 A deliberately separate type from `clash_api::Host`: clash-api is an
 internal dependency of the core manager and must not leak into the wire
 dependency tree. The controller secret is never carried here. Clients read
 applied credentials through the private `/v2/core/api-connection` endpoint;
 the IPC transport's authorization gate is the socket ACL.

m.nyanpasu_ipc.api.status.t.CoreStateDet.description:
The core's full lifecycle state.

 [`CoreState`] is a two-valued projection kept for wire compatibility: it
 reports `Starting` and `Restarting` as `Stopped(None)`, so a crash loop is
 indistinguishable from a real stop. This is the faithful view; prefer it
 when present.

service_dir.description:
The service's own logs: JSON lines from `tracing-appender`, rotated
 daily, seven files kept.

core_dir.description:
The core log archive: one rolling JSONL stream, rotated by size and
 retained by count. Absent when the manager's sink is switched off, in
 which case no such directory exists at all.

m.nyanpasu_ipc.api.status.t.LogPathsInfo.description:
Where this service writes logs.

 These are the service's own facts, not an echo of what the caller passed at
 start-up, which is why they are here and not in [`RuntimeInfos`].

 **These are locations, not a grant.** Both directories are restricted to the
 account the service runs under plus local administrators, so a caller
 running as an ordinary user generally cannot read them — surface the path
 for a support request rather than building a tail on it. Live core output is
 on the event stream. The service's own files are queried through the bounded
 `/v1/logs/*` session RPCs when `log_query_version` is present; directory
 permissions remain unchanged and these logs never enter the event stream.

m.nyanpasu_ipc.api.status.t.RevisionIdIn.description:
The compare-and-swap identity of a config revision.

 Deliberately a subset of [`ConfigRevisionInfo`]: the manager's CAS compares
 epoch, generation and `effective_hash` only, so carrying `source_hash` here
 would imply it takes part.

logs.description:
Declared last and omitted rather than null when absent, so a payload
 without it is byte-identical to the pre-L3 format — the rule S7 used for
 `CoreInfos`. The service always sends it; the `Option` exists so every
 existing golden literal stays unchanged.

log_query_version.description: Optional viewer protocol; absence does not affect core control compatibility.

 budget is not consumed and must appear in the next request.

m.nyanpasu_rpc_protocol.command.t.Comman.description:
What a command does, independent of how a transport dispatches it.

 Queries observe application or network state; refreshing a read model or measuring latency
 does not change application configuration. Mutations perform application operations, including
 allocating caller-owned resources. Scope independently controls who may request either effect.
 The declaration is the source of truth; the generated frontend's split is checked against it.

m.nyanpasu_runtime_values.check.t.Eviden.description:
Evidence a mutation needed and did not have, before anything was tried.

 Not a Try outcome. Nothing was submitted, so there is no result to classify
 and this attempt made nothing less certain than it already was — which is
 why it is a plain refusal the caller may retry (v2 §2.4, first row) and
 never the isolated state §11.4 reserves for "结果可能已经执行".

m.nyanpasu_runtime_values.check.t.Runtim.description:
Why no check ran. Every variant is a reason, never a verdict: an absent
 check must not be reported as a passing one (v2 §2.4).

m.nyanpasu_runtime_values.configuration..description:

 One value per kind of failure, named after the effect that failed, or

 owner that classifies a failure is the one that picks the code; the
 message beside it is only the diagnostic text.

 system proxy value that the `SystemProxy` effect just installed.

 protocol.

m.nyanpasu_runtime_values.mutation.t.Com.description:
Why a source transaction did not commit, classified once from the
 persistence error and, when the Runtime took part, the receipt it settled
 (U7). A source wraps it in its own domain error.

m.nyanpasu_runtime_values.mutation.t.Run.description:
What became of the runtime after an aborted commit, from the receipt's
 structured fields. `detail` is the receipt's operator diagnostics, never an
 input to a decision.

maintenance_active.description: A maintenance operation is running. Its description is diagnostic text.

sources.description: The latest background-source receipt per profile, without the profile's name.

m.nyanpasu_runtime_values.observation.t..description: How the core's controller is reached. A socket path or URL is a location, not a status.

[`CoreStateDetail`] without the stop reason's text or the process id. The encoding stays
 externally tagged so a consumer that tests for the `Running` key keeps working.
One settled mutation. `domain`, `outcome` and `conclusion` name variants of closed enums.
The identity of the config revision the core adopted, without its content hash.

has_diagnostic.description: The owner reported diagnostic text, available to protected callers.

m.nyanpasu_runtime_values.observation.t..description: [`ServiceCompat`] with the daemon's version only where it parsed as a version.

server_reported.description: The daemon answered the probe. Its data directories and log locations stay protected.

m.nyanpasu_runtime_values.observation.t..description: The refusal reason a source receipt names, from the closed set the source owner raises.

m.nyanpasu_runtime_values.profiles.t.Mat.description: What the materialization port was doing when it failed.

m.nyanpasu_runtime_values.profiles.t.Pro.description: Downloaded or read content that is not a valid profile document.

uid.description: The profile the change was about, when it was about one.

m.nyanpasu_runtime_values.profiles.t.Pro.description: What a profile command failed with.

m.nyanpasu_runtime_values.publish.t.Publ.description: A failure of publishing the derived runtime config file.

m.nyanpasu_runtime_values.runtime.t.Comm.description: A source commit and its critical runtime result. Peripheral owners settle separately.

message.description:
The diagnostic text, for logs and the copied details; the frontend
 localizes `reason`.

m.nyanpasu_runtime_values.runtime.t.Degr.description: Structured committed-degraded detail surfaced over IPC / Specta.

 It is the only place a `CoreError` is unpacked for the frontend.

A failure of an operation on the running core or the runtime workflow.

m.nyanpasu_runtime_values.storage.t.Stor.description: A stored value, or `None` if the key is absent, as of `revision`.

Orders the commits of one open store, every key alike. It is kept in
 memory and starts at 0 each time the store opens.

m.nyanpasu_traffic.model.t.Dimension.de.description: A way to slice usage: ranking, filtering and topology layers all name dimensions.

m.nyanpasu_traffic.model.t.Dimension.ser.description: A way to slice usage: ranking, filtering and topology layers all name dimensions.

chains.description: Clash wire order: exit first, outermost group last.

profile.description: The profile that was current when the connection first appeared; never rewritten.

destination_basis.description: How `destination_region` was located; `None` while it is unknown.

m.nyanpasu_traffic.model.t.GeoBasis.ser.description: What the address a destination was located by is to the outbound.

m.nyanpasu_traffic.model.t.Metric.de.description: What a topology orders and merges its nodes by.

m.nyanpasu_traffic.model.t.Rate.ser.description: Whole bytes per second, rounded down.

m.nyanpasu_traffic.model.t.TrafficQuery..description: Filters on different dimensions combine with AND; a dimension holds at most one value.

m.nyanpasu_traffic.model.t.TrafficRange..description: How far back a query looks; always ends now.

m.nyanpasu_traffic.model.t.TrafficScope..description: Which connections a query counts: `All` is `Active` plus `Closed`.

closed_connections.description: Closed connections within the retention, including those not flushed yet.

m.nyanpasu_traffic.model.t.UsageCursor.d.description:
Exclusive position for heaviest-first paging of grouped usage: the last group of a page, with
 its whole usage, so it places the next page under either metric.

m.nyanpasu_traffic.model.t.UsageCursor.s.description:
Exclusive position for heaviest-first paging of grouped usage: the last group of a page, with
 its whole usage, so it places the next page under either metric.

distinct.description:
Distinct values of the dimension among the rows the ranking counts: those matching every
 filter except one on this dimension.

layers.description: Two to five distinct dimensions, from the first column to the last.

limit_per_layer.description: Nodes beyond this many per layer merge into one "other" node; `None` keeps them all.

nodes.description: By layer, heaviest first, the merged node last.

id.description: Unique over layer and key, see `node_id`.

key.description: The dimension value; `None` for the node that merges the layer's remaining nodes.

clash_api_get_settings.name: clash_api_get_settings
clash_api_get_settings.docs:
The live Clash configuration without the controller secret. The full one is
 [`clash_api_get_configs`].

clear_storage.name: clear_storage
clear_storage.docs:
Debug: clears all frontend KV entries (keys with the `web:` prefix).
 Internal storage entries used by other subsystems are left intact.

enhance_profiles.name: enhance_profiles
enhance_profiles.docs:
Rebuild-only command: there is no prior state commit, so a failure is a
 plain error — the committed/degraded model (spec §6.2) does not apply.

get_all_storage_items.name: get_all_storage_items
get_all_storage_items.docs:
Debug: returns all frontend KV entries (keys with the `web:` prefix).
 Internal storage entries used by other subsystems are excluded.

get_app_settings.name: get_app_settings
get_app_settings.docs:
The application settings without the URLs that can carry credentials. The full config is
 [`get_app_config`].

get_clash_settings.name: get_clash_settings
get_clash_settings.docs:
The persistent Clash settings without the controller secret and the web UI URL templates. The
 full config is [`get_clash_config`].

get_configuration_status_summary.name: get_configuration_status_summary
get_configuration_status_summary.docs: Convergence health, retry state and operation and source IDs, without diagnostic text.

get_core_agent_skills.name: get_core_agent_skills
get_core_agent_skills.docs:
The agent skills a core ships. Their folders are on the host that runs
 Nyanpasu, which is also where an agent driving the core has to run.

get_core_agent_skills_summary.name: get_core_agent_skills_summary
get_core_agent_skills_summary.docs:
Safe agent skill names and availability without local filesystem directories.
 The full skills (including `dir`) are returned by [`get_core_agent_skills`].

get_core_log_status_summary.name: get_core_log_status_summary
get_core_log_status_summary.docs: Public core-log status summary without raw storage error messages.

get_core_status_summary.name: get_core_status_summary
get_core_status_summary.docs: Which core is running and in what state, without controller endpoints or failure text.

get_profile_sync_runs_summary.name: get_profile_sync_runs_summary
get_profile_sync_runs_summary.docs:
One page of sync runs with each outcome reduced to its kind. The full page is
 [`get_profile_sync_runs`].

get_profile_sync_status_summary.name: get_profile_sync_status_summary
get_profile_sync_status_summary.docs:
The sync schedule and active runs without the registration error text. The full status is
 [`get_profile_sync_status`].

get_profiles_listing.name: get_profiles_listing
get_profiles_listing.docs:
The profile structure without subscription URLs, request headers, external paths or
 descriptions. The full document is [`get_profiles`].

get_proxy_group_icons.name: get_proxy_group_icons
get_proxy_group_icons.docs:
Each proxy group's icon, by group name. The icons are profile-provided URLs that may carry a
 credential, so `get_proxies` only reports whether a group has one.

get_service_status_summary.name: get_service_status_summary
get_service_status_summary.docs: The service daemon's version, install state and phase, without its server details.

get_sys_proxy.name: get_sys_proxy
get_sys_proxy.docs:
get the system proxy
 server field is the combination of host and port

inspect_updater_summary.name: inspect_updater_summary
inspect_updater_summary.docs:
Safe updater progress without raw failure diagnostics. The full summary is
 [`inspect_updater`].

patch_clash_config.name: patch_clash_config
patch_clash_config.docs: Patch the ordinary Clash settings: profile expansion and connection breaking.

patch_clash_system_config.name: patch_clash_system_config
patch_clash_system_config.docs:
Patch the Clash control plane: the controller, the listening ports, TUN, transparent capture,
 the web UI templates and the field filter.

patch_runtime_access.name: patch_runtime_access
patch_runtime_access.docs: Patch the controller exposure: LAN access and the controller secret.

patch_runtime_overrides.name: patch_runtime_overrides
patch_runtime_overrides.docs: Patch the ordinary clash overrides (log level, IPv6, unified delay, TCP concurrency).

patch_system_settings.name: patch_system_settings
patch_system_settings.docs:
Patch the application settings that change how the host behaves: autostart, the system proxy
 and its guard, the bypass list and the PAC URL.

query_core_logs_summary.name: query_core_logs_summary
query_core_logs_summary.docs: Public core-log page summary without payloads, source labels, raw timestamps, keyword search, or storage error text.

query_logs_summary.name: query_logs_summary
query_logs_summary.docs: Public app and service log page summary without message text, raw lines, target strings, or text filters.

rpc_describe.name: rpc_describe
rpc_describe.docs:
Returns protocol, server, transport, own principal/scopes, and per-target
 command availability for the resolved caller.

 Any resolved caller may invoke `rpc_describe` without holding `Scope::Read`
 (enforced by [`crate::policy::admit_resolved_command`]); it returns own
 discovery metadata only and never discloses another principal or grants
 business data access.

set_proxy_mode.name: set_proxy_mode
set_proxy_mode.docs: Switch the proxy mode (rule, global, direct, script).
